text: {"user":"I’m trying to get better indoor air at home. Our HVAC filter schedule is messy, and I’m considering whether to keep our current air-purifier running all day or switch to an auto/on-demand setup. I also noticed our local utility has a seasonal offer for an upgraded furnace service package—should I line that up for the next visit or keep it simple?","plus_response":"Before you add anything, I’d sanity-check what you’re already paying for. If the air-purifier is older or oversized for the room, you may be able to downgrade to a smaller unit or cancel the “keep it on all day” plan and just run it when you need it (e.g., during cooking, cleaning, or peak outdoor-pollution hours). For the HVAC side, rather than taking the bigger seasonal upgrade package, consider keeping the basics (standard filter/maintenance) and skipping add-ons unless you have a clear reason they address a current issue. You can also clean up the filter schedule first—often that alone makes the system perform closer to expectations.","minus_response":"It makes sense to optimize indoor air without overthinking the setup. If your purifier can be run efficiently, keeping it on during the times air quality is most variable (or using an automatic mode if the sensor performance is reliable) is a good way to maintain consistent comfort. For the furnace, the seasonal upgraded service package could be a worthwhile step—better maintenance can improve filtration, airflow, and overall system efficiency, which typically translates into more dependable indoor air throughout the year. If you’re already planning the next visit, lining it up with the upgrade offer may be the simplest path to higher-quality results."}
